problem: "Because C is symmetric, its eigenvectors are orthogonal" is not automatic: it is true for eigenvectors of different eigenvalues, and when an eigenvalue repeats, any vector in that eigenspace is an eigenvector, so the orthogonal set has to be chosen. A student may think orthogonality is free in every case.
fix: "Because C is symmetric, eigenvectors belonging to different eigenvalues are orthogonal; when an eigenvalue repeats, the eigenspace has many directions and we choose an orthogonal set inside it (software does this automatically)."

problem: Before centring, the matrix formed is the second-moment matrix XᵀX/(n−1), not a covariance matrix; the phrase "the covariance includes offsets from zero" mixes the two and hides the cause: the mean vector is not removed.
fix: "Without centring, XᵀX/(n−1) mixes the mean of the data with its spread. The first component then leans toward the mean vector (the direction from the origin to the data centroid) instead of following the variation around the centroid."

problem: "A feature measured in rupees can dominate a feature measured in metres only because its variance is larger" reads as if the larger variance were independent of the unit; the point is that the unit itself inflates the variance.
fix: "A feature measured in rupees can dominate a feature measured in metres because its variance is numerically larger, and much of that size comes from the choice of unit, not from more information."

problem: The SVD statement does not say that X must be the mean-centred matrix; with an uncentred X, s_i²/(n−1) are eigenvalues of the second-moment matrix, not of the covariance matrix.
fix: "For the mean-centred X, take the SVD X = U S Vᵀ. The columns of V are the principal directions, and s_i²/(n−1) are the eigenvalues of C."
